searchText: What about extra data? such as hard coded pair addresses. Cound also be a solution to the triple nested factory wdym extra data? like data section? adding a specific memory segment to the end of the data section, like solidity does for constant final fields set in the constructor. A string of memory/value pairs makes more sense in a TX, but if it works off of fixed length and it was something like start address/pair count it would be resilient to bad code. _and_ there was no zero compression, just 64 byte sections split into key/value. my idea about this was to just out-line any basic block whose stack height depends on the entry point Not up to date on my complier speak. What is "out-line"? it means to take that block of code and turn it into a function 👍 (outline triggered the part of my brain that says "summarize" not as the converse to in-line) that's the idea about using CALLF(I) for this, not for relaxing stack validation restriction? no, i mean the compiler of the EOF code out-lines it transparently to a separate section? not really, i mean it's like not something the EVM tooling sees it's more like, if you are compiling some EOF code to native code - you generate a `jmp` vs `call` depending on whether the analysis of the EOF code determines the stack height restriction holds or not uhm the goal is to statically verify that there're no stack underflows... somehow you'd need to figure out how many inputs/outputs such outlined block has, and that might depend on other blocks... I don't yet fully imagine how it would work, but maybe interesting direction
